column2: furnished with maidservants, manservants, the raising of banners and household festivals — there, having done as his own teacher said and performed the offering-worship of the Self,
that best of kings meditated in her presence here on the very form of splendour he had seen in a dream at night in his own city.
Having meditated long, the great king gave her many fine garments and divine shrines, and composed a hymn:
Having praised her thus, the king went out with devotion and saw Mahagauri on her right side.
Prostrating himself on the ground like a staff and again praising her, he gave her various costly garments
and great, priceless ornaments. Then, having circumambulated, he went out with his wife,
and having performed a great worship according to the method told by his teacher, he stayed there seven nights, meditating on her alone.
On the eighth day, bowing to the Goddess and gazing at her with devotion, he prayed in his heart, "Mother, grant my desire."
Kamakshi, well pleased, spoke with a voice from the sky: "O king, four sons will be born to you who are portions of me."
Hearing this utterance, his face blooming with joy, having prostrated fully to the supreme Shri, with no other refuge,
taking leave of the Mother in his mind, the son of Indumati returned with his wife and ministers to the city of Ayodhya.
Such is the power of Kamakshi, who desires the good of all worlds; she fully fulfils the wishes of all her devotees.
Many in the worlds, having worshipped this Kamakshi, the supreme deity, duly and with devotion, have obtained all their desires.
Even today the devoted obtain the fruit, O sage, and many more will be objects of Kamakshi's compassionate glance.
Who is able to describe the greatness of this Goddess? Not I, not Shambhu, not Brahma, not Vishnu — how then others?
Thus I have told you something of the radiant conduct of Kamakshi; it is remembered as removing all sins of those who hear and read it.
Then whoever he looks at, speaks to, touches or thinks of comes under his control like a servant, with half his body.
Likewise, O ascetic, a flower, fruit, perfume, drink or garment, over which the mantra has been recited a hundred and eight times, when sent to a woman, draws her at once, her heart bewildered.
In a secluded place one should draw with gorochana on the ground an image, beautiful and adorned with amorous attire and ornaments,
with the great mantra, joined with the birth-name and enclosed within the goad-syllable, placed on its forehead, throat, heart, navel and knees,
having written it with the syllables of Love so that it lies in all the joints of the limbs; then, facing that direction and having made one's body Tripura,
forming the Kshobhini mudra, one should recite the mantra eight hundred times, placing it in the house of fire, full of the light of moon and sun.
Then one should imagine the woman, her glances wavering, tormented by the arrows of Love, her hips throbbing with the blaze of passion,
swallowed up in the circle of Shakti by the whirl of shining rays, her good conduct cast aside, her lotus eyes wide,
her eyes drawn, her composure lost and modesty dissolved, bound by the fetters of mantra, yantra, herbs and the great mudra, her good conduct cast aside, her lotus eyes wide,
reciting the great mantra that surpasses the mind, her garment taken away, as if bewildered, as if agitated, as if scorched, wondrous,
as if painted, as if unconscious, as if churned, as if dissolved, as if motionless, as if become another;
one should imagine the woman whirling in the sky like a bamboo leaf tossed by the whirling wind of the mantra, even from a hundred yojanas away.
Then one should imagine the earth, with its mountains, woods and forests, bounded by the four oceans, blazing in the centre of the chakra.
By six months of practice one becomes like Kama; by a glance he attracts people, by a glance he brings them under control,

by a glance he agitates a woman, by a glance he removes poison, by a glance he makes one a master of speech, by a glance he bewilders all, and by a glance he destroys quartan and other fevers in a moment.
One who wears hidden the chakra drawn with a yellow substance quickly brings about the paralysis of speech of disputants; there is no doubt.
One should also draw it with the juice of the great indigo, joined with the enemy's name; facing south and burning it in the fire, one kills one's enemies.
With buffalo and horse dung and cow's urine, the name inscribed, the chakra placed in sour gruel causes hatred among enemies.
Joining the name with gorochana, placed in the middle with a crow's feather, hanging in that form, it is supremely effective for driving away.
Drawing the chakra with milk, lac, gorochana and the juice of the great indigo and wearing it, one brings the four classes under control.
If by this same method one casts it into water, one gains incomparable good fortune by bathing in and drinking it; there is no doubt.
If one always imagines a land, a city or a beautiful woman placed in the centre of the chakra as blazing, within seven days one agitates it, O sage.
If one draws this chakra in yellow and uses it facing east, one paralyses all disputants.
If one worships it drawn in vermilion colour facing north, the world comes under one's control, not otherwise.
One who draws the chakra with red ochre and worships it facing west becomes able to attract, subdue and agitate all women.
O enemy of the Vindhya's pride, if one worships it alone in secret on a mountain, the mantra-practitioner obtains freedom from age and death; there is no doubt.
This secret has been told; it must be kept hidden, O great sage. Through concealment comes all perfection, and through disclosure only ruin.
One who performs these rites without first doing the preliminary recitation, O sage, incurs the curse of the deity and does not attain perfection.
To remove the faults of such use, the wise should again recite a hundred thousand times and perform worship duly; then the man becomes fit again.
One who, without desire and overflowing with devotion, always worships the deity,
who remains meditating on her alone and recites the mantra as far as he is able —
she herself carries his worldly burden and accomplishes his liberation; ever present with him, she tells him everything.
As an affectionate cow follows her calf, so the Goddess follows her devotee who has taken refuge in her.
Agastya said: O horse-faced one, tell me the meaning of the word "one who has taken refuge," whom Gauri runs after as a cow runs after her calf.
Hayagriva said: The man who has placed his whole burden, of this world and the next, on the Goddess, his mind ever fixed on her,
agreeable to all everywhere, free of all opposition, having no other refuge, earnestly beseeching Gauri for protection,
with the faith that she will protect him, whose one purpose is her service, devoted to worshipping her — that is taking refuge.
Whenever there is praise or blame, "Let people blame, or let them praise" — seeing his own nature with a clear mind, the one who has taken refuge should not give way to dejection or distress.
The resolve to be agreeable, the avoidance of opposition, the faith that she will protect, and the choice of her as protector,
self-surrender and humility — taking refuge is sixfold. Having accepted self-surrender, one should offer the five limbs; there is nothing equal to this as a means to enjoyment and liberation.
Humility, unpretentiousness, non-violence, forbearance, uprightness, service to the teacher, purity, steadfastness and self-control,
dispassion toward sense-objects and absence of egoism, seeing the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain, non-attachment and non-clinging to son, wife, home and the like,
constant evenness of mind in desirable and undesirable events, and unswerving devotion to me with single-minded feeling,
resorting to solitary places, distaste for crowds, constancy in knowledge of the self and insight into the purpose of the knowledge of truth — one should always practise these means of knowledge.
One who does her work, who holds her supreme, who is devoted to her and free from attachment, without enmity toward any being, attains the highest glory.
A teacher, wise like me, is famed, O tormentor of Vatapi; a disciple like you is declared a teacher of the secret tradition.
Forming the hands into a cup, the forefingers shaped like goads, the middle fingers turned downward in reversed order,
in this order, O divine sage, the two younger fingers in the middle of the middle fingers, the ring fingers straight, and the two forefingers outside them,
the thumbs staff-shaped placed at the bend of the middle fingers — this mudra is famed by the name Unmadini, O tormentor of Vatapi.
Placing the two ring fingers of this below, shaped like a goad, one should employ the forefingers too in the same order.
This is the Mahankusha mudra, accomplishing the purpose of every task.

Placing the left arm on the right side and the right on the left, O divine sage, and turning the hands round; the little and ring fingers joined in this order, O ascetic, pressed by the forefingers, with the middle fingers uppermost,
O husband of Lopamudra, one should hold both thumbs fully extended. This is the Khechari mudra, best of the best; by merely knowing it one becomes dear to the Yoginis.
Turning the hands round, touching, shaped like a half-moon, one should then join the pairs of forefingers and thumbs together,
and set below the middle fingers supported by the little fingers; then, joining these bent, with the ring fingers lowest of all — this is the Bija mudra, which quickly brings all perfections.
The tips of the middle fingers bent and placed above the forefingers, the little fingers likewise placed between the ring fingers,
all joined together and pressed by the thumbs — this is the first mudra, named the Yoni mudra.
These mudras, O divine sage, are causes of the Goddess's pleasure; they should be employed at the time of worship in their proper order.
If an auspicious dream is seen, then an excellent meritorious act should be performed; after a bad dream one should recite a thousand and eight times,
and have the worship of Tripurambika performed in the manner described. If no dream is seen at all, then success comes after a long time.
The Goddess should be received with supreme devotion, with more than the remaining digits; at once he becomes a disciple, purifier of those who purify a row of diners.
One should offer body, wealth and life to that revered teacher, remain ever dependent on him, and never slight his word.
One who, when pleased, grants the fortune of liberation in half a moment — know that teacher, who carries one across worldly existence, to be rare.
The syllable "gu" means darkness and "ru" means its remover; because he removes darkness he is called guru.
Having obtained a teacher whose form is knowledge, one should not turn to another teacher; one should regard even a harsh word spoken by the teacher as a blessing.
Whether worldly, Vedic or spiritual, one should take knowledge from him, having first saluted him.
Having thus performed the threefold initiation, one should teach again what is to be done: devotion to the teacher is right conduct, and treachery to him is sin.
Remembrance of his feet is liberation — this is the rule as long as one has a body. The sin one incurs by speaking falsely before the teacher
is not incurred even by killing a cow or a brahmin. "I, whose line of teachers extends from Brahma down to a blade of grass —
for me, who am worthy of worship by all, who on earth is not worthy of worship?" One who is thus agreeable to all is declared a disciple.
Endowed with pure character and many virtues, because he abides by the teacher's instruction he is called a disciple.
Tired of recitation, one should meditate again; tired of meditation, one should recite again. For one engaged in recitation, meditation and the like, the mantra is quickly perfected.
As by the power of meditation even a worm becomes a bee, so by the power of samadhi a man becomes Brahman.
As the world dissolves in time and is no longer seen, so one should close the eyes — this is the mark of meditation.
When the supreme truth, beyond letters and changeless, is known, the mantras together with their presiding lords become servants.
For one established in the sense of oneness with the Self, whatever he does is vision; his glance is yoga, austerity, the mantra and wealth.
When identification with the body has fallen away and the Supreme Self is known, wherever the mind goes, there is samadhi.
One who sees the all-pervading, tranquil, blissful Self without a second has nothing left to attain or to know.
A hymn is equal to a crore of worships; recitation equal to a crore of hymns; meditation equal to a crore of recitations; and absorption equal to a crore of meditations.
The body is declared the temple, and the individual soul is Maheshvara himself. One should discard the stale offering of ignorance and unite with the sense "I am He."
Bound by the husk it is paddy; without the husk it is rice. Bound by fetters the soul is called jiva; freed from fetters it is Maheshvara.
As the path of birds in the sky and of fish in the water is not seen, so is the great conduct of great souls.
One should perform the daily worship by day and the occasional worship by night; rites for desired ends may be done at both — this is the conclusion of scripture.
Above crores upon crores of great gifts, great vows and great sacrifices is the remembrance of the holy sandals of the teacher.
Knowingly or unknowingly, as long as one bears a body, one should observe the conduct of one's class and stage of life for freedom from karma.
Whatever comes from the teacher's mouth is called all scripture; one should do it even if it is forbidden, and never transgress the teacher's command.
Even one rich in caste, learning and wealth, seeing the teacher from afar, should joyfully prostrate once like a staff and circumambulate him three times.
One should bow to every deity, or even a blade of grass, with the thought that it is the teacher; and one should bow to an image of metal or clay with the thought that it is a god.
Those who say "hum" or "tu" to their teacher, who defeat a brahmin in argument, or who reveal the secret scriptures, become brahmarakshasas.
One should always contemplate non-duality, but not non-duality with the teacher; one should not revile other traditions, or the Vedas, scriptures, Agamas and the like.
A disciple living in the same village should bow to the teacher at the three junctions of the day; one living a krosha away should bow to him daily with devotion.
A disciple half a yojana away should bow on the five festival days; from one yojana up to twelve yojanas,
he should bow to the teacher once in as many months as there are yojanas. A disciple living very far away should go whenever he wishes.
One should not approach a king, a deity or a teacher empty-handed; one should offer fruits, flowers, garments and the like according to one's ability.
Clothed in human skin, the supreme Shiva himself secretly wanders the earth to favour good disciples.
To protect true devotees, though formless he takes form; Shiva, the treasury of compassion, acts in the world as if a worldly man.
The revered teacher is declared to be Shiva himself without the third eye, Achyuta without four arms, and Brahma without four faces.
The unfortunate do not see the revered teacher, called the supreme truth, standing before their eyes, as the blind do not see the risen sun.
Reflection on the truth is best, reflection on recitation is middling, reflection on scripture is low, and reflection on worldly matters is lowest of the low.
There is no truth higher than the teacher, no happiness higher than knowledge, no worship higher than devotion, and no fruit higher than liberation.
In all the Vedas and scriptures, in Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and the rest, here and there, Shri Kamakshi, higher than the highest, is spoken of by various words.
Shachi and Indra, Svaha and Agni, Prabha and the Sun, Lakshmi and Narayana, Vani and the Creator, Girija and Shiva,
Agni and Soma, Bindu and Nada, Prakriti and Purusha, the supporter and the supported, enjoyment and liberation,
prana and apana, word and meaning, injunction and prohibition, pleasure and pain — whatever pairs are seen or heard
in all the worlds, all that is the supreme Brahman, without doubt. They know the transcendent supreme light by the name Kamakshi,
on whom Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and others always meditate. Thus whoever abides here in this path of Shakti
is the ground of the Goddess's grace and a vessel of enjoyment and liberation. Those who worship Kamakshi, with mantra or without,
whether women, vaishyas or shudras, attain the supreme goal; how much more kshatriyas and brahmins who worship with mantras!
Though living in the world, they are surely liberated; there is no doubt. An offering of sugar, honey, ghee, plantains and milk-rice
should always be offered on the five festival days; one who is able yet does not worship incurs the Goddess's curse.
If unable, one should always worship Ambika with offerings of the imagination. A householder, observing auspicious conduct,
should worship Mahalakshmi, the great Goddess, with an agreeable wife as companion. The teacher should explain the conduct three times, O pot-born one;
if the disciple does not accept it, the sin is the disciple's and not the teacher's. Lakshmi and Narayana, Vani and the Creator, Girija and Shiva,
the revered teacher, the teacher's wife and one's parents should be contemplated with the mind. Thus I have told everything in brief, O pot-born one;
by attending to this much, one becomes all-knowing and wise.
Having placed the Lady of the chakra and offered the chakra, pervading the body, one should then place the Shakti goddesses beginning with Sarvasankshobhini.
The five short vowels, then the four diphthongs, ha, ya, ra, va and la, a and ka, kha, ga and na at the beginning — this is the order in the remaining groups.
On the forehead and cheeks, on the shoulders, at the base of the feet, on the knees, above and below on the shanks, and likewise in reverse on the left side.
Sha, sha and sa — these are known as the forty-two letters. The first group has five letters, the second four.
The Shakti Sarvasankshobhini, Sarvavidravini, the Shakti Sarvakarshani and Sarvaprahladini,
a five-lettered group in six groups, and the ninth considered three-lettered. Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, the lord of wealth, Indra and Yama in order,
the Shakti Sarvasammohini, Sarvastambhini, the Shakti Sarvajrimbhini and Sarvavashakarini,
Varuna, Soma and the three Shaktis — these nine are declared the lords of the letters; this is the order of the Bhuta script.
Thus in creation the recitation is in this order; in withdrawal it is reversed. The places should be assigned, with visarga and bindu at the end of the letters.
the Shakti Sarvamantramayi and Sarvadvandvakshayankara. Having placed the Lady of the chakra and offered the chakra, pervading the body,
the wise one should then perform the placement of Rati and the others, preceded by meditation: like hibiscus flowers, their bodies red with saffron,
one should then place the ten beginning with Sarvasiddhiprada: in the right nostril, at the root of the teeth, and on the right breast,
seated on the left laps of the Kamas, to be meditated on as bearing arrows and bows. Kama with Rati and Priti is sought as the beloved of Kamini;
on the elbow and wrist, and on the left in reverse order. Sarvasiddhiprada, ever, and Sarvasampatprada,
the radiant Kamanga joined with Mohini follows Kalahapriya; with his amorous ways he is joined with Vilasini.
the goddess Sarvapriyankara, Sarvamangalakarini, the Shakti Sarvaghamochini and Sarvaduhkhavimochini,
Kama joined with Kalpalata; Kamuka with Shyamavarna; Kama with Shuchismita; Bandhaka joined with Vismrita;
Sarvamrityuprashamini, Sarvavighnavinashini, Sarvangasundari and Sarvasaubhagyadayini.
Ramana with Vismitakshi; Rama with Lelihana; Ratinatha with Ramani; Ratipriya rich in sky-garments;
Having placed the Lady of the chakra and offered the chakra, pervading the body, one should then place those beginning with Sarvajna on the chest and at the places of the teeth.
Ratinatha joined with Vama and Kubja, and with Dhara; Ramakanta, Ramopasya, Ramamana, Nishachara;
Sarvajna, Sarvashakti, Sarvajnanaprada, the goddess Sarvajnanamayi, Sarvavyadhivinashini,
Kalyana, lord of Mohini; Nandaka with Uttama; Nandi with Surottama; Nandana and again Nandayita;
Sarvadharasvarupa, Sarvapapahara, the goddess Sarvanandamayi, Sarvarakshasvarupini, and the tenth, to be known as Sarvepsitaphalaprada.
Panchabana joined with Sulavanya; Balanidhishvara; again Ratisakha joined with Kalahapriya;
Having placed the Lady of the chakra and offered the chakra, pervading the body, the wise one, having placed Vama and the others as before, then places Pakshini and the others.
Pushpadhanva with Ekakshi; Sumukhesha; Mahadhanu; Nili; Jadilya; Bhramana; in order, the lord of Palini;
Bhramamana, beloved of Shiva; Bhrama; Bhranta with Mugdha; Bhramaka joined with Rama; Bhramita is called the bee;
Kameshvari should be known as supreme, then Mohini, Vimala, Aruna, Jayini, then Sarveshvari and Kaulini — so their names are told by the wise.
Bhrantachara with Lochana and again with Dirghajihvika; Mohana follows Bhramavaha and Ratipriya;
Having placed the Lady of the chakra and offered the chakra, pervading the body, visualising a triangle in the heart, in the directions beginning with the east in order,
Mohaka with Palashakshi; Moha is sought in Grihini; Vikatesha; Mohadhara; this Vardhana joined with Dhara;
outside it the wise should place the four weapons; in the corners beginning with the south-east, and the four seats in the middle.
Madanatha, the incomparable; Manmatha joined with Malaya; Madaka joined with Hladini, desiring Vishvatomukhi;
Having placed the middle circle, one should place the sixteen Nityas: Kameshvari, the Nitya, the Nitya Bhagamalini,
Nayaka, preceded by Bhringa; Gayaka joined with Nandini; Ganaka to be known with Anamaya; Nartaka is sought with Kali;
the Nitya Nityaklinna, the Nitya Bherundini, the Nitya Vahnivasinika, and Mahavajreshvari,
Kshvellaka rich in Kalakarni; Kandarpa is called Matta; Nartaka beloved of Shyamala; Vilasi joined with Jhasha;
the Nitya Duti, the Nitya Tvarita next, the Nitya Kulasundarika, and after that the Nitya Kulya,
Kamavardhana rejoices on meeting Unmatta. Then, preceded by meditation, one should perform the placement of Shrikantha and the others.
the Nitya Nilapataka, the supreme Nitya Vijaya, and then Mangala, called preceded by Nitya,

Remembering the Ardhanarishvara, half vermilion and half gold, bearing the emblems of the mountain's daughter and Hara, holding two nooses, a rosary, a bracelet and the boon-giving gesture, one should place them on the places of the letters for one's desired aim.
the Nitya Prabhamalinika and the Nitya Chitra likewise; one should place these from the feet to the heart within the triangle.
Shrikantha, Ananta, Sukshma, Trimurti, Amareshvara, Urvisha, Bharabhuti, Atithisha, Sthanuka, Hara,
the Nitya Pramodini and the Nitya Tripurasundari; in their midst one should place the Goddess whose self is the undivided universe.
Chandisha, Bhautika, Sadyojata, Anugraheshvara, Akrura and Mahasena — these are the excellent forms.
Then Krodhisha, Chandisha, Panchantaka, Shivottama, likewise Ekarudra, Kurma, Ekanetra and Chaturanana,
Ajesha, Sharva, Somesha, Hara, Langali, Daruka, Ardhanarishvara, Umakanta, Apadhya and Dandin,
Atri, Mina, Mesha, Lohita, Shikhi, Khadga, Danda, Dvidanda, Sumahakala and Vyalin,
Bhujangesha, Pinaki, Khadgesha, Baka, Shveta, Abhra, Lakulishiva and Samvartaka.
Purnodari, Viraja, the third Shalmali, Lolakshi, Vartulakshi, Dirghaghona,
Sudirghamukhi, Gomukhi, the ninth Dirghajihvika, Kunjari, Urdhvakeshi, Dvimukhi, Vikritanana,
Satya, Lila, Kala and Vidya are the chief vowel-Shaktis; Mahakali and Sarasvati, endowed with all perfections,
Gauri, Trailokyavidya, Mantratmashaktika, Lambodari, Bhutamata, Dravini, Nagari,
Khechari, Manjari, Rupini, Virini, Kotara, Putana, Bhadra, Kali, the Yoginis,
Shankhini, Garjini, Kalaratri, Kurdini, Kapardini, Vajra, Jaya, Sumukheshvari,
Revati, Madhavi, Varuni, Vayavi, another Rakshavadharini, and the one called Sahaja,
Lakshmi, Vyapini and Maya are counted as the Shaktis of the letters. Having formed the limbs with the letters doubled with the young one, and then with the letters alone,
one should perform the sixfold placement to attain the state of the deity. First one should place Vighnesha and the others, preceded by meditation,
like the young sun, elephant-faced, three-eyed, holding noose, goad, boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, accompanied by their Shaktis:
Vighnesha, Vighnaraja, Vinayaka, Shivottama, Vighnakrit, Vighnahanta, Vighnarat, Gananayaka,
Ekadanta, Dvidanta, Gajavaktra, Niranjana, Kapardavan, Dirghamukha, Shankukarna, Vrishadhvaja,
Gananatha, Gajendrasya, Shurpakarna, Trilochana, Lambodara, Mahanada, Chaturmurti, Sadashiva,
Amoda, Durmada, Sumukha, Pramodaka, Ekapada, Dvipada, Shura, Vira, Shanmukha,
the god named Varada, Vakratunda, Dvidantaka, Senani, Gramani, Matta, the one whose mount is the intoxicated mouse,
Jati, Mundi, Khadgi, Varenya, Vrishaketana, Bhangyapriya, Ganesha, Meghanada and Ganeshvara —
these are the Ganeshas of the fifty-one letters in order. Shri, Hri, Pushti, Shanti, Tushti, Sarasvati,
Rati, Medha, Kanti, Kamini, Mohini, Tivra, Jvalini, Nanda, Suyasha, Kamarupini,
Ugra, Tejovati, Satya, Vighneshani, Svarupini, Kamarta, Madajihva, Vikata, Ghurnitanana,
Bhuti, Bhumi, Dviramya, Amarupa, Makaradhvaja, Vikarna, Bhrukuti, Lajja, Dirghaghona, Dhanurdhari,
Yamini, Ratri, Chandrakanta, Shashiprabha, Lolakshi, Chapala, Rijvi, Durbhaga, Subhaga, Shiva,
Durga, Guhapriya, Kali and Kalajihva are the Shaktis. Then, attentive, one should perform the placement of the planets, preceded by meditation,

with hands showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, their bodies embraced by their Shaktis, one should remember the Sun and the others as resembling saffron, milk, blood, jasmine, gold and conch,
and clouds, smoke and darkness. Placing the Sun below the heart, the Moon on the head, Mars on the eyes,
Venus on the heart, Mercury in the middle of the heart, Jupiter on the throat, Saturn on the navel, Rahu on the mouth and Ketu on both feet.
Then, meditating, one should place the stars, resembling the blazing fire of doom, with hands showing boon and fearlessness, adorned with all ornaments,
on the forehead, the eyes, both ears, both nostrils, the throat, both shoulders, then the elbows and wrists,
the breasts, navel, hips, thighs, knees, shanks and both feet. Then the placement of the Yoginis should be done: in the Vishuddha and in the heart,
in the navel, the Svadhishthana, the root centre, between the brows and on the crown in order; in the centre of the moon-pericarp of the lotus, and the letter-Shaktis on the petals,
and at the tips of the petals of the lotus on the head one should place them all: Amrita, Nandini, Indrani, Ishani, Atyuma,
Urdhvakeshi, Riddhividushi, Lrikarika, Ekapadatmika, Aishvaryakarini, Aushadhatmika,
Ambika and Rakshatmika — these are the sixteen Shaktis. Kalika, Khechari, Gayatri, Ghantadharini,
Nadatmika, Chamunda, Chhatrika, Jaya, Jhankarini, Sanjna, and after that Tankahasta,
and Tankarini — these twelve Shaktis should be known in order. Dankari, Tankarini, Namini, Tamasi,
Thankarini, Daya, Dhatri, Nadini, Parvati and Phatkarini should be known as Shaktis, two serpents,
Vardhini, Bhadra, Majja, Yashasvini, Rama and Lamini — these six Shaktis in order,
Narada, Shri, Shandha and Shashvati — four Shaktis; likewise two, Hakini and Kshama.
Then on the foot, the genitals, the belly, the heart, the arms and the head, from the right to the end of the left foot, one should place the signs of the zodiac beginning with Aries.
Then one should mentally place the fifty-one seats as one chakra: Varanasi, Kamarupa, Nepala, Paundravardhana,
Varasthira, Kanyakubja, Purnashaila, Arbuda, Amratakeshvara, Ekamra, Trisrotas, Kamakoshthaka,
Kailasa, Bhrigunagara, Kedara, Chandrapushkara, Shripitha, Ekavira, Jalandhra, Malava,
Kulanna, Devikota, Gokarna, Marutesvara, Attahasa, Viraja, Rajaveshma, Mahapatha,
Kolapura, Kailapura, Kaleshvara, Jayantika, Ujjayini, Chitra, Kshiraka, Hastinapura,
Udira, Prayaga, Shashtimayapura, Gaurisha, Salaya, Shrishaila and Maru,
then Girivara, then Mahendra, the Vamana mountain, then Hiranyapura and Mahalakshmipura,
and Purodyana and Chhayakshetra, as the wise declare. One should place them, joined with the order of the script, on the places of the letters,
and the others in the places stated, joined in the sequence of the script. The sixfold placement has been explained by me, as spoken by the Lord himself.
One whose body has been placed in this way becomes the embodiment of the deity. Then, having first done the sixfold placement, one should perform the placement of the Shrichakra.
With the mantras from Amsha to Anandyamurti one should perform the pervading placement, and place the Lady of the chakra and the mantras of offering the chakra in the heart.
In the other places as stated one should place Ganapati and the others, the left equal to the right thigh, placing all in order:
Ganesha, Kshetrapala, the Yogini and Batuka. First Indra and the others should be placed at the tips of both big toes,
at the sides of the knees, shoulders, crown, mouth, sides and knees and on the crown; then in the root centre the ten perfections beginning with Anima
are to be placed on the shoulders, arms, back and chest, on the insteps and buttocks, on the arms and back, and on the head and both feet in order:
Anima, Laghima, the third Mahima, Ishitva, Vashitva, Prakamya and Prapti, Ichchhasiddhi, Rasasiddhi and Mokshasiddhi, as they are remembered.
Then, O brahmin, the wise one should place the eight Mothers in order: on the two big toes, on the right side, on the head from the left,
on the left knee and the right knee, and on the right and left shoulders.
The one whose form draws faith, the one whose form draws the self, the one declared to draw nectar, and the one who draws the body.
The Shakti Sarvaranjini, Sarvonmadini, the Shakti Sarvarthasadhini and Sarvashapurini.
On the right chin, the throat, the breast, the navel and both sides; Vama, Vinodini, Vidya, Vashita and Kamiki are considered.
Having placed the Lady of the chakra in the heart and lifted up the chakra, showing the mudra called Yoni, one should recite the Sarvananda mantra.
Thus one becomes the chakra-goddess of one's own chakra.
In these holy and charming regions, adorned with Vidyadharas and frequented by Gandharvas, Yakshas and immortals, the three-eyed god sported with the Goddess.
Surrounded by the gods with Indra, by sages, Yakshas and Siddhas, by Gandharvas, Vidyadharas and chief Daityas and all others of various kinds, Shambhu found joy on that mountain.
There the Apsarases dance for the lord of the gods, the hosts of Gandharvas sing with delight, and some play divine instruments while others quickly praise the best of gods.
Thus that great-souled god, the slayer of Bhaga's eyes, accompanied by his own mighty hosts equal to Shakra, Yama and Agni, did not leave the mountain, for the Goddess's pleasure.
While the Lord, the destroyer of Kama, stayed there with the Goddess, what did Mahadeva do? We wish to know this.
On the peak of the Himalaya, the Lord, wishing to please the Goddess, again and again made her laugh with his Ganas of various shapes.
The one marked with the crescent moon delighted the Goddess and sported with the glorious, omniscient, auspicious ones able to take any form.
Then the supreme Goddess went alone to her mother, who was seated on a bright, wondrous golden seat.
Seeing the virtuous Goddess arrive in divine form, Mena, beloved of Himavan, honoured the blameless one with a costly seat, and when she was seated, said to her:

Tell me, daughter of lovely eyes, why you have come after so long. You play, united with your husband, with poor amusements.
brahmapuran:38:27	Those who are poor and without shelter, Uma, play just as your husband does, dear one.
Thus addressed by her mother, she was not pleased in mind; endowed with great forbearance, she said nothing to her. Then, dismissed by her mother, she went and spoke to the god:
O Lord, god of gods, I will not live on this mountain. Make another dwelling for me somewhere in the worlds, O radiant one.

Though I always urged you about a dwelling, O mistress, you never liked any other dwelling, O Goddess.
brahmapuran:38:31	Why now do you yourself seek a dwelling elsewhere, O lovely one? Tell me that, O sweetly smiling Goddess.
Then the god laughed and, to make the Goddess laugh, the Lord said:

It is just so, no doubt; why are you angry? I wear a hide, I am without a dwelling, and I live in the cremation ground.
brahmapuran:38:37	Homeless, I wander in forests and mountain caves, surrounded by naked hosts, O lotus-eyed one.
brahmapuran:38:38	Do not be angry with your mother, O Goddess; your mother told you the truth. For creatures on earth there is no kinsman equal to a mother.
I have nothing to do with kinsmen, O lord of the best of gods. Act, Mahadeva, so that I may obtain happiness.
Hearing the Goddess's words, the lord of the gods, for her pleasure, left his mountain and went to Meru, frequented by gods and Siddhas, with his wife and his hosts.
Having said this, the brahmin sage spoke again to Daksha:
Why do you not worship the Lord, the master of creatures, who is worthy of worship?
I have many Rudras, bearing tridents and with matted hair, stationed in eleven places; we know no other Maheshvara.
This one mantra is for all, yet my Lord has not been invited. As I see no deity higher than Shankara, so this vast sacrifice of Daksha will not come to be.
Various shares have been given to Vishnu, and shares given to the Rudras; the other gods too have their own shares; but I give no share to Shankara.
Knowing that the deities had gone, the daughter of the king of mountains then spoke to Sharva, the god, the lord of creatures, her husband:
O Lord, where are these gods led by Shakra going? Tell me truly, O knower of truth; this is my great doubt.
O illustrious one, Daksha, the excellent lord of creatures, is performing a horse sacrifice; the heaven-dwellers are going there.
O illustrious one, why do you not go to this sacrifice? By what prohibition is your going ruled out?

O illustrious one, the gods themselves have arranged all this: in all their sacrifices no share has been assigned to me.
brahmapuran:39:39	O fair one, one must go by the path followed of old; the gods do not give me a share of the sacrifice according to dharma.

O Lord, among all the gods you are superior in power and virtues, unconquerable and unassailable in splendour, fame and glory.
brahmapuran:39:41	But through this exclusion from the share, O illustrious one, I have fallen into great sorrow, and I tremble greatly.
brahmapuran:39:42	What gift, observance or austerity should I perform so that my husband, the inconceivable Lord, may today obtain a share in the sacrifice made splendid by Indra and the other immortals?
As she spoke thus, the Lord reflected and, delighted, said to his agitated wife: "You do not know me, O Goddess of slender waist; what kind of speech is this of yours?
I know, O wide-eyed one, and all the good know through meditation: today through your delusion the gods with Indra and all the three worlds are ruined.
They praise me constantly as lord of the sacrifice; they sing the Rathantara Saman for me; brahmins worship me with Vedic mantras; my Adhvaryu priests assign me a share."
You boast like an ordinary man in an assembly of women; you praise yourself and are proud of yourself, no doubt.
I do not praise myself, O Queen of gods; as you follow along, I will create one for the sake of the share, O lovely one of fine hips.
Having said this to his wife Uma, dearer to him than life, the Lord created from his mouth a being born of the fire of wrath,
and said to him, "Go to Daksha's sacrifice, O great lord; destroy Daksha's rite quickly with my permission."
Then, sent by Rudra, in the guise of a lion, playfully, knowing it was caused by the Goddess's wrath, he destroyed Daksha's sacrifice.
And through her wrath the very terrible Bhadrakali, the great Goddess, went with him and his followers as witness of her own act.
He is that Lord Wrath, who makes his abode among the dead, famed as Virabhadra, who wiped away the Goddess's anger.
From the pores of his own body he created lords of hosts, followers of Rudra, fierce hosts with Rudra's might and valour.
All were Rudra's attendants, all of Rudra's valour; they rushed down swiftly in hundreds and thousands.
Then, O brahmins, a very great "kilikila" sound, made by all the hosts of Rudra, arose as if filling the sky.
By that great sound all the heaven-dwellers were terrified; the mountains crumbled and the earth trembled.
